title: AI Data Analyst: What It Is & How To Choose One In 2026
summary: An AI data analyst takes a business question, finds the governed data, runs the analysis and explains the answer with its work shown. Plus a 12-point checklist.
body_markdown:
## The 12-point checklist for evaluating an AI data analyst


Run these checks on your data, with your questions and the people who will use the tool. Each point says what to test and what passes, then our evidence for Dot. Our playbook turns them into a 50-question eval set with thresholds, then shows how to[run a two-to-four-week pilot and send an RFP checklist](https://www.getdot.ai/blog/ai-data-analyst-playbook) .


### Accuracy and reasoning


1.


**Accuracy on your own questions.** Ask about 50 questions whose answers you already trust, taken from dashboards nobody argues with, and score each one against a tolerance you set before the first run. Ask a few of them three different ways and require the same number every time.


*Evidence:* on Adyen's DABstep benchmark, a configured Dot answered 90% of a 30-task slice of easy and hard questions, scored with DABstep's own scorer. The same write-up puts Google's Data Science Agent, the strongest public agent at the time, at around 52% (weighted overall, November 2025, as our[pricing page](https://www.getdot.ai/pricing) also cites), and trained Adyen analysts near 62% on the easier tasks after three or more hours of work. A 30-task slice is not your warehouse, which is why this check uses your own questions.


2.


**Reasoning past a single query.** Include "why" and what-if questions that need several queries, and check that the numbers in the explanation reconcile with each other and with your dashboards.


*Evidence:* on DABstep, learning the warehouse's unwritten conventions took Dot to about 30%; the rest needed counterfactuals, multi-tier comparisons and joins that do not fit into one SQL statement ([the write-up](https://www.getdot.ai/blog/from-10-to-90-percent-on-adyens-dabstep) ). At KRY, one open-ended question led to more than 20 hypotheses tested and a revenue opportunity of €800K a year identified and sized in 10 minutes ([case study](https://www.getdot.ai/impact/kry) ).


3.


**Improves when you configure it, and proves it.** Take three wrong answers, fix the context behind them, and rerun the whole eval. A pass is a before-and-after score per question, with nothing that used to pass now failing.


*Evidence:* on DABstep the model stayed the same; the configuration around it took Dot from 10% to 90% on the slice. In the product,[Train](https://www.getdot.ai/changelog/2026-09-01-train-dot) tests Dot against your trusted answers, fixes notes, relationships and table docs in an isolated environment, and reports accuracy before and after. Evaluations rerun on demand, including from CI.


4.


**Asks before it guesses.** Put five or six ambiguous questions in the eval, such as "what's our churn rate?" when you track both logo and revenue churn. A pass is one short question back, or an answer that says which reading it used. A fail is a confident number for one reading with no mention of the other.


*Evidence:* Dot asks clarifying questions in the[Duolingo](https://www.getdot.ai/impact/duolingo) and[Choco](https://www.getdot.ai/impact/choco) rollouts. An answer that rests on a choice your workspace does not settle, such as an undefined metric, is marked "Assumption made" with what it assumed ([how that works](https://www.getdot.ai/context-agent) ).


### Trust and governance


1.


**Shows its work.** Can the asker see the SQL, tables and definitions behind any answer, and can an analyst trace the number to its source?


*Evidence:* since August 2026 every Dot answer can show its[lineage](https://www.getdot.ai/changelog/2026-08-01-answer-lineage) : a map from the warehouse tables through the exact SQL to the answer, dbt models included, plus any team note that steered the query.


2.


**Leaves an audit trail in your own logs.** Take one query from your warehouse's query history and ask the vendor to trace it to the person and conversation behind it.


*Evidence:* every SQL query Dot runs carries a comment naming the user, the workspace, the trigger (a question, a schedule or a dashboard refresh) and a link to the chat; on BigQuery these also land as job labels in INFORMATION_SCHEMA and the billing export. Enterprise plans add audit logs of user actions and data access ([security](https://www.getdot.ai/security) ).


3.


**Uses your semantic layer instead of re-deriving it.** Ask for three metrics defined in your semantic layer and compare the answers with your BI tool's numbers for the same filters and dates.


*Evidence:* Dot answers through your[LookML](https://www.getdot.ai/integrations/looker) , the[dbt](https://www.getdot.ai/integrations/dbt) Semantic Layer,[Cube](https://www.getdot.ai/integrations/cube) ,[Malloy](https://www.getdot.ai/integrations/malloy) and[Power BI semantic models](https://www.getdot.ai/integrations/power-bi) rather than writing its own versions of your measures, and since August 2026 it applies each Looker explore's default filters instead of overriding them.


4.


**Governs changes to context.** Who can change what "active customer" means? Check that every change is reviewed, versioned, testable before it goes live, and reversible.


*Evidence:* Dot's[Context Agent](https://www.getdot.ai/context-agent) pulls definitions from dbt, BI tools and docs, but nothing goes live on its own: each change is a proposal with a readable diff that you can test in its own environment, merge in part or reject, and every file keeps its history. Environments can mirror to Git for teams that want pull requests.


### Security, delivery and cost


1.


**Enforces permissions and row-level security.** Sign in as a regional manager and ask for revenue by country, then for a table that person cannot see. A pass is their rows only and a refusal on the restricted table, in every channel.


*Evidence:* Dot applies the warehouse's own permissions and row-level security, with role-based access inside Dot, and in MCP clients answers with the user's existing Dot permissions. The Team plan and above add SSO (Okta, Entra ID, Google) and Dot's own row-level rules, which can key on user attributes synced from Looker. A user with no value is denied rather than shown everything, and "Test as user" previews the exact filter a person's queries would carry ([September 2026 release](https://www.getdot.ai/changelog/2026-09-01-train-dot) ).


2.


**Handles data and prompts safely.** Ask where the data goes, which LLM providers see prompts, what they retain, and for the audit report.


*Evidence:* Dot queries your warehouse in place and surfaces only the results you request; no data is copied or moved. All LLM providers run with zero data retention, and prompts are never stored or used for training. Dot is SOC 2 Type II and GDPR compliant, with EU data processing and a DPA ([security and trust](https://www.getdot.ai/security) ).


3.


**Works where questions are already asked.** Check that the agent is where your pilot users ask data questions today.


*Evidence:* Dot answers in[Slack](https://www.getdot.ai/integrations/slack) ,[Microsoft Teams](https://www.getdot.ai/integrations/microsoft-teams) , email, its web app and[MCP clients](https://www.getdot.ai/integrations/mcp) such as Claude, ChatGPT and Cursor, and turns a recurring question into a schedule. Placement drives use: Ramp's analyst agent, which lives in Slack, answered 1,476 questions in four weeks while their old #help-data channel answered 66 ([Ramp engineering](https://engineering.ramp.com/post/meet-ramp-research) ). We compare the chat tools in AI data analysts for Slack and Teams.


4.


**Costs scale with use, and can be capped.** Estimate the cost per answered question at pilot volume and at ten times that, and check whether you can cap spend per person or team. Per-seat pricing makes you decide who may ask. Usage pricing makes you decide how much asking is worth.


*Evidence:* as of October 2026, Dot has unlimited users and bills on credits (usage), not seats. Free is $0 with 300 one-time credits and full Pro features. Pro is $180/month billed annually ($200 month-to-month) with 150 credits/month. Team is $720/month billed annually ($800 month-to-month) with 800 credits/month. Enterprise is custom. Admins can set weekly credit limits per user or as shared group pools, and decide who may use each model tier ([pricing](https://www.getdot.ai/pricing) ).


## Will an AI data analyst replace your analysts?


It replaces the queue, not the people who know what the numbers mean. I wrote the long version in[Will AI replace data analysts? A data founder's perspective](https://www.getdot.ai/blog/will-ai-replace-data-analysts-a-data-founders-pers) . The evidence since then adds three things.


- **Demand grows when asking gets cheap** (Ramp, check 11), and every answer still rests on a definition someone has to own.
- **Accuracy decays unless someone tends it.** Anthropic's own analytics agent lost accuracy within a month as the data model kept changing ([the playbook](https://www.getdot.ai/blog/ai-data-analyst-playbook) has the numbers and the weekly routine that catches it). Keeping context true is analyst work.
- **Analysts move up the stack.** In our case studies, Duolingo's analysts "reclaim time for deeper modeling and experimentation", and Choco's analytics team moved its time to "architectural and structural data problems."


The analyst who answered "what was revenue in EMEA last month?" ten times a week now owns the definition of revenue, reviews the agent's context changes, keeps the eval set current, and takes the questions that need judgment. A role that only pulled the same numbers from the same tables does shrink, and it is better to say so plainly.
